Test locally first. Use the live Gorbagana network only for a small smoke test after local checks pass.

## Testing path

Use this path before you deploy or upgrade a program.

1. Run local program tests.
2. Run a local validator or fast program-test layer when the test needs chain state.
3. Review accounts, signers, PDAs, CPIs, and authorities.
4. Run one small live Gorbagana smoke test.
5. Inspect the signature, logs, accounts, and fee payer in the explorer.

<Callout type="warn" title="Local tests are not Gorbagana devnet">
  `solana-test-validator`, Bankrun, LiteSVM, and Mollusk are local testing tools. They do not mean Gorbagana has a public devnet, testnet, faucet, or airdrop.
</Callout>

## Choose a test layer

Pick the smallest layer that can prove the behavior you care about.

<Accordions type="multiple">
<Accordion title="anchor test">

Use for Anchor workspace integration tests.

- Proves: your Anchor tests build, deploy locally, and pass against a local validator.
- Does not prove: live Gorbagana funding, RPC behavior, or explorer visibility.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="anchor test --skip-local-validator">

Use when you already run a local validator.

- Proves: your tests run against the local validator process you control.
- Does not prove: public network behavior.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="solana-test-validator">

Use for local CLI and client loops.

- Proves: transactions, accounts, logs, and deploys work against a local Solana-compatible validator.
- Does not prove: Gorbagana network state or live fees.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Bankrun">

Use for JavaScript or TypeScript program tests.

- Proves: program instructions can run against an in-process bank-style test environment.
- Does not prove: public RPC behavior or wallet UX.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="LiteSVM">

Use for fast local SVM tests.

- Proves: program logic can be tested without a full validator process.
- Does not prove: public network behavior.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Mollusk">

Use for isolated instruction checks.

- Proves: instruction-level behavior and account validation can be tested directly.
- Does not prove: full app flow or wallet behavior.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Live Gorbagana smoke test">

Use as the final minimal check after local tests.

- Proves: the funded wallet, RPC endpoint, transaction, and explorer verification path work together.
- Does not prove: security review, performance, or production readiness.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Anchor local tests

For Anchor workspaces, start with the standard local test flow.

```bash
anchor test
```

Anchor builds the workspace, starts a local validator, deploys the program locally, runs the tests, and stops the validator.

Use `--skip-local-validator` only when you already run a local validator yourself.

```bash
anchor test --skip-local-validator
```

Keep tests close to the accounts your program expects. Check signers, writable accounts, PDA seeds and bumps, token accounts, and error paths.

## Local validator loop

Use a local validator when you want to run CLI commands, frontend scripts, or manual transactions before touching the live network.

Terminal 1:

```bash
solana-test-validator
```

Terminal 2:

```bash
solana config set --url localhost
solana config get
solana balance
```

Deploy locally when you need to inspect program logs or account behavior.

```bash
cargo build-sbf
solana program deploy ./target/deploy/PROGRAM.so
```

After local checks pass, point the CLI back to Gorbagana before any live smoke test.

```bash
solana config set --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

## Fast program tests

Fast local tools are useful when you want tighter feedback than a full validator loop.

| Tool | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Bankrun | JavaScript and TypeScript tests that process transactions against loaded programs and accounts |
| LiteSVM | Fast local SVM program tests |
| Mollusk | Instruction-level tests for program behavior and account validation |

Use the upstream docs for each tool's setup and API. Keep Gorbagana docs focused on what changes for the live network: RPC, native GOR, bridge, explorer, and wallet flow.

## Live Gorbagana smoke test

Run one small live check only after local tests pass.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Point clients at Gorbagana

```bash
solana config set --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
solana config get
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Check the fee payer

```bash
solana address
solana balance
```

The wallet must hold native GOR.

</Step>
<Step>

### Submit a small transaction

Use the smallest safe action for your project: a tiny transfer, a no-risk instruction, or a deployment to a throwaway program ID.

```bash
solana transfer RECIPIENT_ADDRESS 0.001 \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Confirm the signature

```bash
solana confirm TRANSACTION_SIGNATURE -v \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Inspect in the explorer

Open the [Explorer](/docs/network/explorer) and check the signature, status, logs, fee payer, account changes, and fee.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warn" title="Do not reuse old signed transactions">
  If a transaction expires or fails before landing, create and sign it again with a fresh blockhash.
</Callout>

## CI notes

Run local tests in CI. Keep live Gorbagana checks out of default pull-request jobs unless you intentionally manage funded test wallets.

Use CI for:

- `anchor test`
- unit tests and instruction tests
- TypeScript client tests that do not need live funds
- linting and type checks

Avoid putting live private keys or funded wallets in default CI jobs. If you add a live smoke job, keep it manual, small, and easy to audit.
